summary.year_convention: Main year is the cited publication year, not automatically the first-public or confirmation year. Preprint dates are version submission dates; journal-only dates use publication dates.
summary.scope: Earliest located target-specific public sources, not a claim of exhaustive historical priority. Earlier unpublished attributions and same-day reports are distinguished.

confirmation.detail: DES J0246-1845: Table 1, Fig. 5 and Table 9; adaptive-optics imaging reveals the deflector.

records.note: GraL V section 4.1 leaves J0246-1845 as a possible lens (binarity not excluded). Lemon et al. confirm it with spectroscopy and AO imaging. Both preprints were submitted on 2019-12-19; no within-day priority is assigned. Dates here are arXiv submission dates, not observation dates.

records.note: Earliest verified candidate: Spiniello et al. 2018 v1, KIDS0907+0003 (Possible NIQ). Chan et al. 2020 also lists it as a candidate, without X-shooter follow-up. GraL V (2019) reports a lens identification, but its Keck spectrum is unresolved and no deflector is detected. The authors' identification is retained as a distinct event; an independent confirmation publication was not established in this review.

confirmation.detail: Lens model and counterimage interpretation; not the 1991 infrared-object discovery.

records.note: Rowan-Robinson 1991 discovers the infrared object, not its lens nature. Matthews 1994 is the earliest located explicit lens hypothesis, which those authors disfavor; Elston 1994 gives a positive possible-magnification interpretation. Broadhurst & Lehar 1995 and Graham & Liu 1995 supply lens/counterimage evidence; Eisenhardt 1996 adds HST confirmation (preprint 1995). Do not treat the 1994 hypothesis as confirmation.

primary.detail: Lists SDSS J1138+0314 and credits Burles et al. in preparation.

records.note: Earliest located public listing is Oguri et al. (2005), available as a 2004 preprint; it already calls the object a lens and credits Burles et al. in preparation. Eigenbrod 2006 measures the deflector redshift and is not the discovery paper. SQLS II describes the Magellan snapshot discovery but still cites an unpublished Burles manuscript. Original discovery/confirmation publication priority remains unresolved; Sluse 2012 later publishes resolved image spectra.

primary.detail: Describes SDSS J1226-0006 and credits Inada et al. 2002, submitted.

records.note: Pindor 2003 already reports J1226-0006 as a discovered lens, but credits Inada et al. 2002 (submitted). That manuscript was not located as a public publication; its year must not be used as a verified public discovery date. Inada 2008 is a later SQLS sample report, and Sluse 2012 supplies the first published individual-image spectra. Original discovery/confirmation authorship remains unresolved.

records.note: Khramtsov 2019 Table 4 lists KIDSJ1359+0129 at 13:59:43.98, +01:28:13.90, matching this catalogue position. Jaelani 2021 instead confirms SDSS J135944.21+012809.8 at (209.9342, +1.4693), about 5.5 arcsec away. The inherited name/coordinates and full alias therefore disagree. Do not transfer Jaelani's confirmation, redshift or paper-image identity to the KiDS candidate without reconciling this discrepancy. The inherited scientific values and image pixels are retained, but their association is explicitly unverified.
